items.text: WTI and Brent crude surged ~9% and ~8% respectively on Aug 31–Sep 1, tracking escalation fears in the Middle East. Elevated geopolitical risk and supply concerns are driving energy shocks that could feed back into inflation expectations, which are already sticky at 4%+ year-ahead in consumer surveys.

Aug payroll gains of 162K were robust, but initial claims crept to 206K and wage growth (AHE 3.09%) has cooled meaningfully. The services employment index contracted for a second straight month (47.8), signaling labor market softening and pressure on household income at a moment when consumers are already sentiment-constrained.

Core CPI and core PCE remain elevated at 2.47% and 3.34% YoY (July), while headline inflation has moderated to 3.3%. However, year-ahead inflation expectations jumped to 4.3% in Aug amid energy shock and policy uncertainty. For credit, sticky core and elevated expectations signal the Fed is unlikely to cut rates aggressively; term premiums and curve risk remain live.

Fed held at 3.75% on Sep 4; the 2-10 curve steepened to 43bps from 39bps, reflecting uncertainty over the growth-inflation mix and geopolitical tail risks. ECB is on pause at 2.25% (June hike), signaling a higher-for-longer stance in Europe. Divergence between sticky core inflation and labor softening creates policy dilemma that may keep rates elevated longer.

HY OAS at 265 and IG OAS at 81 remain relatively tight given the macro crosscurrents (energy shock, sentiment collapse, labor softening). CCC-rated spreads at 1051bps show marginal stress but not crisis mode. Energy shocks and uncertainty around business outlooks (business conditions expectations down 11-17%) are beginning to stress lower-rated credits; watch for widening in lower quartiles.

GDPNow tracking ~4.7% for Q3, but this appears flattered by tariff pull-forward and retail anomalies. Underlying momentum is challenged: housing starts down to 1.239M (from 1.415M), existing home sales soft at 4.06M, and mortgage rates at 6.71%. Q1 actual GDP was only 1.5%, and forward indicators (China PMI at 49.8, U.S. ISM Mfg at 54.6) show deceleration. Growth relief is fragile.

Consumer sentiment crashed to 51.7 (Aug final) from 55.2 (July), driven by geopolitical fears, energy prices above $4/gal, and elevated inflation expectations. Housing is under pressure (starts and existing sales declining), mortgage affordability is strained at 6.71%, and savings rate ticked up to 3.0%, signaling precautionary behavior. Lower/middle-income cohorts and Republicans hit hardest—risk of demand destruction in Q4.

themeCards.title: Middle East Energy Supply Risk
themeCards.statusLine: WTI +9.8%, Brent +8.9% on Aug 31–Sep 1 amid Iran escalation. Geopolitical tail risk is now front-and-center, with consumers already pricing higher year-ahead inflation (4.3%) and expected gasoline prices ($4.00+ realized).
themeCards.relevance: For special situations, energy/credit correlation is sharp: energy exporters (HY energy spreads), refiners/transport, and low-income consumer credits are all at risk. Refinancing walls in distressed energy credits could blow out. Commodity-linked derivative stress is a secondary concern.

themeCards.title: Consumer Sentiment Cliff / Demand Destruction
themeCards.statusLine: Michigan sentiment collapsed to 51.7 (Aug final) from 55.2 (July), down 11% YoY, driven by inflation fears and economic outlook deterioration. Vulnerability is concentrated in lower-income, older, Republican, and less-educated cohorts—exactly the groups most exposed to cost-of-living shocks.
themeCards.relevance: Special situations credit must monitor consumer cyclicals (retail, discretionary, subprime auto/credit cards). Mid-market consumer credit could see stress waves in Q4 if sentiment remains depressed. Watch for defaults and covenant pressure in consumer-linked credits.

themeCards.title: Labor Market Divergence / Softening
themeCards.statusLine: Services employment index fell to 47.8 (Aug, second contraction), AHE decelerated to 3.09%, and claims rose to 206K. Manufacturing is still solid, but services (67% of GDP) show cracks. Gap between headline payroll strength and underlying labor indicators is widening.
themeCards.relevance: Weak services employment and wage deceleration threaten consumer balance sheets and limit pricing power for labor-intensive credits (hospitality, retail, business services). Refinancing pressure on leveraged operators in services/retail will mount if wage growth doesn't recover.

themeCards.title: Sticky Core Inflation + Policy Uncertainty
themeCards.statusLine: Core CPI at 2.47%, core PCE at 3.34%; year-ahead inflation expectations jumped to 4.3% despite headline cooling. Policy uncertainty (Iran conflict, tariff debate, mid-cycle dynamics) extends duration risk and pushes term premiums higher. Fed is on hold, not ready to cut aggressively.
themeCards.relevance: For special situations, sticky core means real yields stay elevated, pushing down valuations on long-duration, low-coupon credits. Refinancing risk is acute for 2024–2026 maturity cohorts. Commodity-linked bonds and inflation-sensitive credits face headwinds. Watch CCCC spreads for stress signals.

themeCards.title: Housing / Real Estate Stress
themeCards.statusLine: Housing starts fell to 1.239M (July), existing home sales at 4.06M (down from 4.13M), mortgage rates at 6.71%. Affordability is collapsing; origination volumes are cooling. Fed has no easy pivot to support housing given inflation.
themeCards.relevance: Residential real estate credit, REIT credits, construction/materials, and mortgage servicers face sequential deterioration. Refinancing risk for developers is mounting. Watch for stress in residential construction debt, both senior and subordinated. Cross-default contagion into equity sponsors is a tail risk.

themeCards.title: China Manufacturing Contraction / Global Demand
themeCards.statusLine: China PMI at 49.8 (Aug), still in contraction for 2nd month, though new orders/production returning to growth (>50). Services and small firms remain weak. Reflects uneven recovery and policy hesitation; large firms holding up, but breadth is lacking.
themeCards.relevance: For special situations, China contraction signals weaker global demand for industrial/cyclical exports and commodities. U.S. exporters and commodity-linked credits face headwinds. Tech/semiconductor supply chains (high-tech sub-index >52) are bright spot, but auto, materials, and generalist industrials will struggle. Watch for stress in cyclical/trade-sensitive leverage.

regime.label: Stagflationary crosscurrents
regime.detail: elevated energy shocks, sticky core inflation, consumer sentiment cliff, labor softening, Fed on hold, geopolitical tail risk.
